summary: Iteration 4: tested owner-account protection and the new Activity Log (API and UI), plus a regression check. Backend: the new test_owner_activity.py passed 20 of 20. The full suite passed 96 of 96 with 1 skip, after I fixed 2 stale tests. Frontend Playwright on prevent-restore.preview.emergentagent.com, logged in as the non-owner QA admin (ID 17): the owner badge and 'Protected owner account' show, and the owner row has no reset or toggle buttons. Each Activity Log filter works (search, admin, area, action, from/to), as do Reset, the empty state, pagination, editor links (and no link on delete entries), and the details text. The Admins create/reset/deactivate flow writes the matching 3 activity entries, and the Blogs 'Last updated by' column still works. No critical or functional bugs found.

minor.issue: Impossible calendar dates (Feb 30/31) are accepted: JS Date rolls them over to Mar 2/3 and returns 200 instead of 422. Values like '2026-01-01T10:00' that are not YYYY-MM-DD are accepted too.
from > to is not checked and just returns an empty list. The from/to day boundaries are UTC (T00:00Z to T23:59Z), not the admin's local day, so entries near midnight can land on the 'wrong' day.

issues: From/To use the browser's native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of a styled calendar component
The tiny inline 'From'/'To' labels sit beside the inputs, are not aligned with the other filters and look cramped
Leftover deactivated TEST admins created by test runs (IDs 19-26) clutter the list. Clean up with the CLI snippet in test_credentials.md.

action_items: Optional: return 422 for impossible dates in the activity filters, e.g. check that new Date(v).toISOString().slice(0,10) === v
Optional: decide whether the from/to filters should use the admin's timezone, or document that they are UTC
Optional: replace the native date inputs on the Activity Log with the app's styled date picker and tidy the From/To labels
Clean up the TEST_ admins, blogs (trashed TEST_Act Blog entries) and activity rows before going live
critical_code_review_comments: test_cms_api.py logged in as the REAL OWNER (v3mtechnology@gmail.com) with an outdated password. Every run counted as failed logins against the owner and could trigger the 5-attempt lockout. I changed it to the QA admin.

Owner protection is checked before the transaction in setStatus/resetPassword. That is fine, because isOwner cannot be changed through the API. There is no way to transfer ownership (CLI or API), which you may want to note for operations.
The reorder log has no entityId or entityLabel (only details.count), so the log can't show which items moved. Consider storing the before/after id order.
Deleting an already-trashed item logs a second 'delete' entry (remove() doesn't check deletedAt)
listActivity passes action/entityType through as free strings, which is fine (Prisma parameterises them). The limit is silently capped at 100.
